paragraphs: HopSkipDrive arranges rides for students who cannot be served by a traditional school bus route. The company calls itself a technology company that solves complex transportation challenges where there is a heightened need for safety, equity, and care.

Rides come through a marketplace connecting kids, older adults, or anyone needing extra support to highly vetted caregivers on wheels. The homepage says rides are licensed, regulated, and ready in six hours. Ride types span McKinney-Vento, foster care, special needs and IEPs, charter schools, general education, after school, and career and technical education. Districts also use RouteWise AI, which optimizes routes for buses and small vehicles.

Denver Public Schools is described on the site as using RouteWise AI to optimize its multimodal transportation system. Cypress-Fairbanks Independent School District decided to outsource its McKinney-Vento and a portion of foster transportation to the company. Counties, government agencies, and nonprofits are also named as groups the company supports. It traces its start to three working moms trying to get their busy kids to and from school and activities.
